subject: Mixing numerical and categorical item responses with MIRT

messages.author: 73fb61795976b321
messages.subject: Mixing numerical and categorical item responses with MIRT
parts:
Hello all,

I was wondering how to build a latent variable that takes into account both numerical and categorical item responses with MIRT.

https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/mirt/versions/1.33.2/topics/mirt

I am aware that we can mix item types by passing a vector to the itemtype argument of the MIRT function. What is the appropriate item type to use when one item has linear (or polynominal?)  relationship with the factor? An graded item type with infinite categories would do?

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Hugo


--

messages.author: 73fb61795976b321
messages.subject: Re: Mixing numerical and categorical item responses with MIRT
parts:
Hello all,

Do you think this would be a reasonable approach? Suppose I have three different types of items and I want to build a latent variable out of a combination of the three.

_OC - indicating ordinal categorical item
_NC - indicating nominal categorical item
_N   - indicating numerical item

First, I am thinking of creating a latent variable combining only categorical items using MIRT.

y1 =f (I1_OC,I2_NC,I3_NC, I4_OC, I5_NC, etc.)

and then, creating a second latent variable combining my numerical items with y1 latent variable using lavaan or some other SEM software.

y2 = f(I6_N, I7_N, y1)

Any concerns about this approach?

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Hugo

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Mixing numerical and categorical item responses with MIRT
parts:
I don't think there's anything inherently wrong about this, but it's likely inefficient and wouldn't lend itself to kosher model-based inferences (like SEs or Wald/LR tests). It might be best just to model everything in lavaan, or to use the categorization approach you described in the earlier post (hard to say which is better, as it would depend on many factors....). HTH, and sorry for the delayed replies!

Phil
